title.narrative: Improved Resource Mobilization and Utilization Reform Program, Subprogram 2

description.narrative:
The proposed Improved Domestic Resource Mobilization Reform Program aligns with the Government of Pakistan's efforts to implement macroeconomic reforms, mobilize resources and promote public financial management (PFM) for economic growth. The core of the program is domestic resource mobilization (DRM). However, considering Pakistan's development context and the program's overarching goal of fiscal consolidation, DRM is interpreted more broadly, consistent with the 2015 Addis Ababa Action Agenda.
The Subprogram 2 will be utilizing two financing options: (1) Conventional PBL. OCR loan of $300 million for sovereign budget support; and (2) Policy-based guarantee. $500 million partial credit guarantee (PCG) backed by a sovereign counter indemnity, to mobilize commercial financing of $1 billion.

Outcome: By 30 June 2026:
Tax revenue as a share of gross domestic product (GDP) improved to at least 12% of GDP (2022 baseline: 10.1% of GDP). Source: Finance Division, MOF: Fiscal Operations, 2021-2022.
Description: 1.1 In order to improve taxpayer integrity and compliance, Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) approved the Inland Revenue (IR) Strategic Reform Plan (SRP) 2021-2025, which addresses the weaknesses identified in the Tax Administration Diagnostic Assessment Tool (TADAT) 2021, and implemented the following priority actions from the plan: (i) conducted and published the tax gap analysis for core taxes (Federal level Income Tax, Sales Tax, and Customs Duty); (ii) established a sectoral benchmark working committee, approved a benchmark study for inputs outputs, energy use, and value addition of the textile sector, and issued an office order to upgrade the automated system “FASTER” by incorporating benchmarks and input/output ratios to ensure certainty, transparency and truthfulness in processing of FBR sales tax refunds and issuance of valid and legitimate refunds to exporters; (iii) submitted for stakeholder consultations the approved draft amendments to the income tax, sales tax, sales tax on services in Islamabad Capital Territory, and federal excise duty that will harmonize and streamline core processes and procedures for tax administration. (iv) conducted and published findings of a specially designed independent third-party survey to monitor taxpayer perceptions regarding access to, and quality of, FBR products and services for the corporate sector (at least 10% of respondents are women-led companies).

Description: 1.2 To promote digital transformation and automation in tax administration, FBR implemented the following actions to introduce and operationalize the Synchronized Withholding Administration and Payment System (SWAPS): (i) established the legal framework to implement SWAPS through the National Assembly's approval of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001 (Amendment); (ii) established the Directorate General of Digital Initiatives and began operationalization by deploying a Director General and four Deputy Directors; (iii) developed and approved an integrated application programming interface (API) that will enable synchronized withholding tax transactions and digital payments to multiple stakeholders in real-time and commenced engagement with Habib Bank, Bank Islami, and Bank Alfalah as model withholding agents for implementation of SWAPS; and (iv) approved and commenced implementation of an Information and Cybersecurity Governance Framework to upgrade its cyber security architecture.
